summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, obstructive sleep apnea, asthma, and obesity, was admitted for acute-on-chronic neck pain that worsened over three days and was associated with headache, dizziness, nausea, and one episode of vomiting. He initially left the ED after receiving IV hydromorphone and starting a prednisone taper but returned due to pain exacerbation during a bumpy car ride. Imaging of the head and neck showed no acute intracranial hemorrhage, dissection, or vascular occlusion, though evaluation was limited by artifact. He was managed with continued home medications including OxyContin, oxycodone, prednisone, and lidocaine patch, while ketorolac was discontinued due to GI discomfort. Ibuprofen was held due to NSAID allergy and GI risk. Nausea resolved, and he tolerated a regular diet. He was discharged stable with instructions to follow up with his primary care provider for medication tapering, mood concerns, and monitoring of chronic anemia.
